# Page 3^page=3
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Course objectives • Overview of the principles and techniques of software engineering • Compared to basic SE courses, SE2 focuses on development of complex systems (large-scale projects) • Topics: • Software lifecycles, standards, project management and metrics • Specification languages: UML, Alloy • Requirements analysis • Software architecture and implementation platforms • Validation and verification SE2 - Logistics 3

# Page 8^page=8
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Assessment: constraints • Exam is passed if • You get the minimum for each building block • Total is ≥ 18 • Total ≥ 31 (before rounding) = 30L • Important note • R&DD, I&T, RP, quizzes will be assigned only during this winter session SE2 - Logistics 8

# Page 9^page=9
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi R&DD Project • Goals • Put into practice most of the approaches and principles presented in class • Produce high-quality requirements and design documentation • R&DD is a group activity • Students will autonomously form groups • 3 students at most, 1 student (singleton) is also ok (but not encouraged!) • Each student can have a specific role (to be declared during the exam) • But all must have broader knowledge, that is, they must be aware of what the other teammates have done (see later) • Some exercise sessions are dedicated to introducing and discussing the project development • Ad-hoc meetings can be scheduled as required by the groups SE2 - Logistics 9

# Page 10^page=10
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Implementation and Testing (I&T) • Only for groups of two or three students who have taken R&DD • These must be the same groups as for R&DD! • You can choose to continue with I&T after completing R&DD • Goals • Achieve a running prototype implementation offering some of the functionality of the project • Test your prototype possibly using some of the automation tools that will be presented in class • Evaluate through acceptance testing the prototype implemented by another group SE2 - Logistics 10

# Page 11^page=11
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi R&DD and I&T evaluation • We will assess • Quality of the produced artifacts • Project discussion • Ability to justify and soundness of design decisions • Ability to explain rationales • Ability to coordinate with the other group members • Ability to meet the deadlines SE2 - Logistics 11

# Page 12^page=12
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi R&DD and I&T — Important dates • Project assignment: 9/10/2026 • Group registration: 23/10/2026 • RASD submission deadline: 23/12/2026 • DD submission deadline: 06/01/2027 • I&T deliverable deadline: 31/01/2027 • Acceptance testing deliverable deadline: 07/02/2027 • Final project presentations (to be scheduled) SE2 - Logistics 12

# Page 13^page=13
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi R&DD and I&T — Notes • You can submit before the deadlines, if you want/need! • When you submit a deliverable, you can also submit a new, improved/updated version of the previous deliverables • make sure to document what changes you applied SE2 - Logistics 13

# Page 14^page=14
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Quizzes on RASD and DD SE2 - Logistics 14 Process overview for each quiz (RASD and DD) Students review docs RASD/DD of past project Quiz administered during a class in-class discussion Evaluation (up to 1 point each)

# Page 15^page=15
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Quizzes on RASD and DD • During the semester we will provide you with (anonymized) past projects (RASD and DD) • Tentative schedule: RASD in mid-October / DD in the first part of November • You review the documentation at home • In class, you fill out a quiz (multiple choices) with questions that concern aspects of the documents you checked (e.g., what kind of errors they contained) • One quiz for the RASD, one for the DD • We will provide an example, concerning a different RASD/DD, to give you an idea of the kinds of questions you can expect • Then we will discuss it during an exercise session • The goal of the exercise is to understand how to/not to create a RASD and DD • Answering each quiz is worth up to 1 point → 2 points can be earned taking both quizzes (one for requirements, one for design) • The quizzes will be administered only once, during the semester • If you do not attend the quizzes, you miss 2 of the total 32 possible point SE2 - Logistics 15

# Page 16^page=16
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi Research Project (RP) • Goals • Get involved into research teams of the DeepSE (software engineering) group • Contribute to the development of novel techniques/tools for research purposes • RPs will be agreed with your instructors: we will schedule a dedicated meeting for this around mid-October • They must be completed by September 2027 at the latest • M.Sc. theses are available, possibly (not only) as continuation of RP SE2 - Logistics 16

# Page 17^page=17
M Camilli, E Di Nitto, M Rossi WE1 and WE2 • Written Exams (WE) focus on all topics presented in the course • Duration: 1h30m each • WE1: 3 exercises on all course topics • WE2: mimics the writing of R&DD • Given a short description of an application, identify requirements, define architecture • Note: scoring well in WE2 requires a good level of experience in writing R&DD documents! • WE1 and WE2 are “open book” • You can use your notes and books SE2 - Logistics 17
